CHIEF COMPLAINT
Upper respiratory infection symptoms.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Randy Gutierrez is a 5-year-old male who presents with upper respiratory illness symptoms that began last night around supper time. Parent reports runny nose and nasal congestion with clear nasal discharge. Patient also has a cough that is not barky in nature. Parent notes patient has been pulling on his ears and rubbing his nose frequently. Rectal temperature measured at 100.3°F this morning. Appetite has been variable—ate approximately 7 ounces from bottle this morning but refused additional bottle and cereal. Patient appears energetic but irritable and is having difficulty sleeping. Parent notes sweating episode this morning. Recent sick exposures include older sister who is currently ill and a playdate with nephew who had a sinus infection.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for runny nose, nasal congestion with clear discharge, nonproductive cough, ear pulling, nasal rubbing, low-grade fever, decreased appetite, irritability, and difficulty sleeping. Also has worsening cradle cap. Negative for barky cough.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Cradle cap.

MEDICATIONS
Tylenol given early this morning for fever. Saline nasal mist applied. Baby Vick's applied to feet last night. Humidifier used at home.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Older sister currently experiencing similar upper respiratory illness symptoms.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recent sick contact with older sister and nephew with sinus infection.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. Ears: Within normal limits. General: Patient alert and cooperative during exam.

RESULTS
COVID-19: Negative.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Viral upper respiratory infection with low-grade fever. Plan to continue supportive care including fluids and rest. No antibiotics indicated at this time. Prescribed sister's cough medication to have on hand; if barky cough develops, give half teaspoon for five days. If no barky cough develops, do not use medication. May use Zarbee's for regular cough using pediatric under-one-year dosing. Counseled regarding no honey for patients under one year; agave acceptable alternative. For cradle cap: Start Head & Shoulders, Selsun Blue, or Nizoral AD (regular strength, not extra strength) twice weekly with soft brush and baby oil for scale removal; avoid contact with eyes during rinsing. Follow-up appointment in one week. Return sooner or call if condition worsens, particularly if barky cough develops.
